incidents.summary: BBC Watchdog reported animal mistreatment at Pets at Home stores; a subsequent BBC clarification concerned the omission of the company's responses from an online version.

sources.title: Pets at Home
sources.quote: The programme discovered evidence of mistreatment of small animals, dead fish being left to rot and be eaten in tanks, and sick small animals up for sale.

sources.title: Pets at Home
sources.quote: The BBC trust published a clarification on 7 June 2016 that the website included a version of the item made before Pets at Home's points in reply to criticisms were incorporated.

incidents.summary: Pets at Home withdrew KONG rope dog leads pending investigation after owners reported that a lead released their puppy, which was then killed by a van.

sources.title: Pets At Home Withdraws KONG Dog Leads Following Puppy’s Tragic Death - Top Class Actions United Kingdom
sources.quote: Pets At Home has withdrawn three KONG rope dog leads after a puppy wearing one of the leads broke loose and was killed by a van.

sources.title: Pets At Home Withdraws KONG Dog Leads Following Puppy’s Tragic Death - Top Class Actions United Kingdom
sources.quote: Within hours of the couple’s contact, Pets At Home reportedly withdrew every KONG rope dog lead from all of its stores pending an investigation into the lead.

positives: Pets at Home worked with IBM and the BRC to test and refine a framework for more accurate supply-chain emissions reporting and wider ESG-risk visibility.
A 1.25MWp rooftop solar array was installed at Pets at Home's National Distribution Centre.
Pets at Home's distribution-centre building received an Excellent BREEAM rating for its environmentally focused design.
Pets at Home achieved a 44% reduction in absolute location-based Scope 1 and 2 emissions since 2016.
